For any nonzero contract balance and when the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient), the reference transfers the entire balance away so address(c).balance == 0 afterward; the mutant that sends only half the balance leaves a nonzero balance and thus violates this property for some inputs.

For any nonzero deposit and when owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the reference C sends the entire contract balance to recipient (so recipient's balance increases by exactly the contract prior balance), whereas the mutant sends only half so recipient's balance increases by less than the full prior balance for some inputs.

If the caller is the owner and the contract has a positive balance, then withdrawAll either succeeds and transfers all Ether out of the contract (leaving contract balance zero) or it reverts — but it cannot silently return success while leaving a nonzero contract balance.

For any caller and any recipient, when owner calls withdrawAll the reference contract always transfers the entire contract balance out (leaving address(c).balance == 0), whereas the mutant that ignores the success of a low-level call can leave funds in the contract when the recipient's fallback reverts, so address(c).balance may remain > 0 for some inputs.
